survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes the problem as a minimum-cost Steiner tree and applies subset dynamic programming over the critical flags.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The pairwise targets are reachable through arbitrary sequences of purchased two-flag toggles, so all critical flags must lie in one purchased connected component.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its shown approach records only a critical-endpoint mask for each edge and appears to discard edges with no immediate critical endpoint, thereby missing useful Steiner/intermediate vertices and paths.
It models the task through independent shortest paths between critical pairs; that does not correctly account for the shared-edge cost structure of one minimum Steiner tree.
Its shown graph/Dijkstra approach similarly treats pairwise shortest-path distances as sufficient, which can overpay for overlapping paths and does not solve the shared-subgraph Steiner optimization.
